---
title: "Surgical Smoke Removal in Laparoscopic Video"
description: "A domain adaptation study testing whether a CNN built for outdoor haze removal transfers to surgical smoke"
date: 2026-08-08
categories: [computer vision, deep learning, domain adaptation]
---

## Overview

Investigated the transferability of AOD-Net, a CNN originally designed for
outdoor atmospheric haze removal, to surgical smoke removal on real paired
laparoscopic footage from the DesmokeData dataset (MICCAI 2024).

## Approach

Designed and implemented a full evaluation protocol — PSNR and SSIM on
held-out validation data — benchmarked against published dehazing baselines,
to test whether a model trained on a visually similar but physically
different problem (outdoor haze vs. surgical smoke) generalizes without
retraining.

## Key Finding
| Smoke density | N | Mean PSNR | Mean SSIM |
|---|---|---|---|
| Low | 32 | 22.99 dB | 0.8088 |
| Medium | 31 | 22.31 dB | 0.7751 |
| High | 33 | 16.52 dB | 0.6346 |

A density-stratified analysis revealed a systematic ~6.5 dB PSNR performance
gap between light and dense smoke conditions — smoke density itself is a
confound the base architecture doesn't account for, not just a difficulty
gradient it handles gracefully.

![Before/after smoke removal comparision along with ground truth](validation-comparison-grid.png)

## Implications

The results point to two concrete next steps for improving robustness in
surgical desmoking: increasing architecture capacity and using
density-aware training strategies, rather than assuming a haze-removal
model transfers as-is.
